title: Optimal-Restriction Five-Sets and Global Cut Stability in Triangle-Free Graph Bipartization
description: Version 0.3.0 of a reproducible computational and structural study of five-vertex induction for triangle-free graph bipartization. The v3 release introduces an exact global cut-stability audit on a saved canonical corpus of 19,270 n=15 graphs. Every saved graph admits a five-set Y with d(G)-d(G-Y) <= 5 such that some maximum cut of G restricts to a maximum cut of G-Y. The same property holds for all 5,337 saved graphs with L(G) >= 12, all 2,103 saved graphs with d(G) > 5, and all seven exactly identified edge-critical saved graphs. The release includes the v3 research note, global-cut landscape code, compact H0 witness tables, extension-frontier diagnostics, optimal-face projection diagnostics, sample checkpoints, and portable validation tests. The full Erdős triangle-free bipartization conjecture remains open, and the saved corpus is not claimed to exhaust all triangle-free graphs on 15 vertices.
